discovery: Quantum simulation of many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Ignacio Cirac
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics, Garching, Germany

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum many-body physics
motivation: Zoller and Cirac showed theoretically that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise Hubbard-type Hamiltonians with fully controllable parameters, and proposed laser-controlled atoms as programmable quantum simulators (Jaksch et al. 1998). Bloch realised this vision experimentally, observing the superfluid to Mott-insulator quantum phase transition (Greiner et al. 2002) and later developing single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopy, many-body localisation and fermionic Hubbard physics. Together they turned Feynman's idea of quantum simulation into a mature laboratory discipline. Their work created the conceptual and technical framework now used worldwide, from lattice clocks and dipolar molecules to Rydberg arrays and neutral-atom quantum processors. It is a rare case of theory and experiment advancing in close dialogue over decades, establishing entirely new ways to study strongly correlated quantum matter with precision and control that were previously unimaginable.
